visualReview.notes: Actually inspected 92 final images: 17 portable, 17 shared-surface, 33 medium-fi and 25 normal terrain-placement views. Compared the stepped tower/palace/Burgrave layout, roof hoardings, Marian lantern, round palace turret, timber bridge and climbing curtain/approach route with the inspected southeast and southwest reference photographs and 1889 published plan. Removed provisional filled court platforms. Rebased separate buildings to reconstructed floors on retained bare-earth data. Fixed inward-facing foundation rings: their previously invisible walls made buildings appear to float. New exterior feet close those gaps. Current Great Tower keeps its 60 m base-to-main-roof span plus small finials. Exact floor levels, window rhythms, stairs and historic roof detail remain approximations.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Six shared graphs: granite, limestone, lime plaster, timber, painted metal and slate. Carved stone shares tinted limestone; recesses share tinted plaster; glazing uses opaque local PBR. Skyline bakes common linear material means into one draw. Six current GLBs contain no embedded images. The inspected shared fixture reads each graph once and unloads to zero live model geometries. Its flat stage exposes foundations and is not evidence of hillside contact. No source photographs were copied as textures.

mediumFiReview.notes: Actually inspected all 33 final medium-fi frames: noon/late light, economy/high settings, 12 architecture cameras, whole-castle four-level comparisons and transitions. District retains tower/palace/Burgrave silhouettes, signed component arrangement, mapped feet, open gate, roof lantern and elevated timber deck at 3968 triangles. Street and close-up add grouped openings, hoarding brackets, timber braces and clipped slate relief. Skyline retains main masses, mapped foundations and clear passages at 900 triangles; small windows, crenellations and stair treads are deliberately absent. Level transitions preserve the site composition. Synthetic outer context is not real village/forest evidence; bounded terrain display is independently checked through normal placement.

fidelityReview.notes: Accepted medium-fi exterior reconstruction. Original 556934-triangle, 46864188-byte master remains exactly reproducible at sha256:2094e82b6eb86b1ab78993df6cc09a84d5a65e8fd2f108cb34bf698c82150b85 from the unchanged karlstejn-castle-model.mjs recipe. Independent browser source retains the evidence-guided exterior and replaces the old provisional terrace model. Official owner history gives 60 m Great Tower height and ascending castle arrangement. Photos guide restored forms; the 1889 plan guides topology before later restoration. Floor estimates, Marian/Palace heights, covered passage decks, steep stairs and foundation exposure need architectural survey for greater accuracy. Interior chapels/artworks, figurative carving, exact crenellations, village and forest are omitted or simplified. Bare-earth acquisition is described as 2009–2013; interpolation under occupied buildings and host terrain vintage remain limits. No ellipsoidal datum conversion or physical-device performance claim.

legacyFidelityScope.notes: Maximum fidelity remains pending. Individual roof silhouettes and mapped component positions are authored, but measured elevations, window layouts on obscured faces and nineteenth-century restoration details need refinement. Official 60 m Great Tower height differs from OSM 53 m. The seven-meter exposed-base interpretation and stepped terrace elevations are provisional, not a survey. The Burgrave roof junctions, palace loggia, gatehouse portals, wall crenellation spacing, dormers and chimney positions use photograph-derived proportions. Interior artworks and rooms are outside this exterior asset. Covered bridges are separate raised structures with visible space beneath. Their deck elevations, support details and stairs require on-site dimensions. Shared plaster, wood, slate and stone graphs avoid embedded images. Shingle relief, masonry joints and wood boards are procedural details; existing stone surfaces need material-specific weathering. Foundation terraces are local contact geometry, not the full castle hill. Approach terrain, surrounding forest and buildings beyond the precinct are excluded.
legacyFidelityScope.reviewBinding: Historical record only; current approval is the newly inspected medium-fi scope.

geometryValidation.notes: Three focused tests pass: original master bytes reproduce independently; current source/runtime hashes and retained raster hash agree; signed map-frame helper accepts fresh identity and direction. Four browser levels retain open court, north gate and empty space below the timber skyway. Near-level mapped foundation rays require outward front faces, matching browser raycasting and detecting the repaired winding defect. Rebuilds reproduce exact LOD bytes within 1000/4000/16000/64000 triangles, eight draws and 3 MB initial download. POSITION/NORMAL use separate 12-byte streams. All six GLBs pass Khronos with zero errors, warnings and images; strict medium-fi findings are empty. Normal placement verifies relative anchor elevation, three ground probes, near-level mapped foundations, open gate at all levels and five clean unloads. These checks sample the reconstruction; they are not exhaustive manifold or architectural survey certification.

terrainReview.notes: Actually inspected 25 final images: five terrain cameras for source and four browser levels. Normal semantic placement uses signed heading and terrainReference; origin elevation is zero within 0.1 mm against the retained native grid. Three open-ground probes differ by less than 0.08 m from triangulated ground. Near levels close sampled mapped foundation faces; north gate stays open at all levels; five unloads restore terrain and leave zero model geometries. Retained 512 m public DMR5G raster and bounded 400 m resampled native grid use Bpv heights, not ellipsoidal heights. Working floor levels, upper/lower stairs, exposed occupied feet and passage elevations are terrain-guided reconstruction. The coarse ground surface smooths steps/retaining edges and interpolates under buildings. This does not survey architectural floors or validate every host terrain product. ČÚZK CC-BY-4.0 attribution and original raster hash are retained.
